title: Scripture and the Holy Spirit
searchTerms: Word of God and the Holy Spirit
definition: Scripture and the Holy Spirit belong together because the Spirit inspired the Word, illuminates the Word, and uses the Word to sanctify God's people.
summary: The Spirit does not lead believers away from Scripture but deeper into its truth, conviction, comfort, and obedience.
christFocus: The Spirit glorifies Christ through Scripture by revealing His beauty, applying His Gospel, and forming His people into His likeness.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Scripture and the Holy Spirit teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to scripture and the holy spirit by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
